$comment: The trail's stops (GAME_DESIGN 12.1, 12.2): S3's two sample stops at the Sol Duc trailhead and the button between stops; S5's sample stops at Deer Lake and the rim, and the trail frame's chrome (the status line, the caption, the toolbar, the (i) square; the strip's mile is a number format, fmt.mile_marker); S6's sample fork at the rim, its outcomes, and the odds' words: the tags, the confirm, the intros (8.7), the Why sheet (12.11), the compass's spoken result (8.8), the outcome's ornaments and pencil rows (12.13). S15a's tailgate and S9's cards replace the sample stops. Drafts until B004 and B005 are answered; preview only.

trail.walk_on.ctx: Every trail stop's button to the next stop (GAME_DESIGN 12.1)

trail.next.ctx: The death box's one button, in place of Walk on (GAME_DESIGN 9.5, 12.17: DRAFT Next); from S24a it leads to YOU PERISHED, and in S6's stand-in to the guest book

trail.sol_duc_trailhead.lot.text: The road ends in a ring of giant trees. You smell wet moss and the river.
trail.sol_duc_trailhead.lot.ctx: Sol Duc trailhead, the first stop: the road's end, where the loop starts

trail.sol_duc_trailhead.trail_mouth.text: The trail slips between two huge trunks. Sol Duc Falls is under a mile in.
trail.sol_duc_trailhead.trail_mouth.ctx: Sol Duc trailhead, the second stop: the trail into the trees toward the falls (0.8 mi)

trail.deer_lake_rim.deer_lake.text: A still lake ringed with firs: the last sure water before the crest. Clouds are building over the Divide.
trail.deer_lake_rim.deer_lake.ctx: S5's sample stop at Deer Lake, the first lake on the climb to the High Divide (GAME_DESIGN 4.3: the last sure water before the dry crest); from S6 it also names the storm the fork's diamond prices (9.5: a danger that can kill is named at an earlier stop)

trail.deer_lake_rim.rim.text: The ground falls away into a bowl of pale rock and heather. You count the lakes twice and get two answers.
trail.deer_lake_rim.rim.ctx: S5's sample stop at the rim of the Seven Lakes Basin, looking down into it (4.3: far more than seven lakes)

trail.caption.ctx: The caption under the picture: the trip's day, the place, its elevation in feet as fmt.ft words it (12.2)

trail.status.sound_on.ctx: The status line's Sound toggle while sound is on, on the cabin first, then on the trail; tap turns it off (12.2, 13.11; King's Quest's own words)

trail.status.sound_off.ctx: The status line's Sound toggle while sound is off, on the cabin and the trail

trail.status.menu.ctx: The ≡ button's spoken name on the trail, and the name of the sheet it opens there (at the cabin the same sheet is the mailbox, home.place.mailbox); its module, the status line, is the cabin's too

trail.toolbar.pack.ctx: The toolbar's first button: what's in the pack (12.2)

trail.toolbar.map.ctx: The toolbar's second button: the park map with your route (12.2)

trail.toolbar.log.ctx: The toolbar's third button: the hiker's log, day by day (12.2)

trail.choice.why.ctx: The (i) square's spoken name: it opens the Why sheet behind a choice's odds (12.1, 12.11)

trail.look.group.ctx: VoiceOver's name for the picture's Look buttons, as a group (12.1, 12.2: tap the picture to Look)

trail.box.more.ctx: The spoken name of the box's continuation mark, in its corner when its words go on in a second box (12.1: never a scroll): the lockbox's and the guest book's box on the porch first, then the trail's

trail.deer_lake_rim.fork.text: Thunder rolls along the Divide, early. The stone staircase drops into the basin; the crest runs on, open to the sky.
trail.deer_lake_rim.fork.ctx: S6's sample fork at the rim of the Seven Lakes Basin: the storm has come early (GAME_DESIGN B.6, 12.12), and the three choices are below

trail.deer_lake_rim.fork.high.ctx: The fork's diamond: on along the open crest past Bogachiel Peak to Heart Lake, in the storm (B.6). Fits the SE with its tag

trail.deer_lake_rim.fork.basin.ctx: The fork's %: down the stone staircase into the basin, to Lunch Lake (B.3)

trail.deer_lake_rim.fork.car.ctx: The fork's sure choice: back down the way you came, to the Sol Duc trailhead (6.9 mi)

trail.deer_lake_rim.fork.high.fail.ctx: The diamond's fail word on its second line, in red: 35% hit (lightning hits close). Must fit the SE's line (T02c)

trail.deer_lake_rim.fork.high.badly.text: If it goes badly: lightning hits close, on the highest ground for miles.
trail.deer_lake_rim.fork.high.badly.ctx: Why sheet: what the fail band means for Stay high (12.11, 8.7)

trail.deer_lake_rim.fork.basin.badly.text: If it goes badly: a slip on the stairs. A bruise, at worst a turned ankle.
trail.deer_lake_rim.fork.basin.badly.ctx: Why sheet: what the fail band means for the staircase

trail.deer_lake_rim.fork.high.clean.text: The storm walks off north along the ridges and leaves you the crest. You come down to Heart Lake with your hair still on end.
trail.deer_lake_rim.fork.high.clean.ctx: Outcome: Stay high, clean (good): Heart Lake about 4:26 pm (12.13)

trail.deer_lake_rim.fork.high.shaky.text: You spend twenty long minutes crouched in the krummholz while the sky argues with itself. Then it moves on, and so do you.
trail.deer_lake_rim.fork.high.shaky.ctx: Outcome: Stay high, shaky (a mishap, +20 min): Heart Lake about 4:46 pm

trail.deer_lake_rim.fork.high.struck.text: Lightning hits the ridge a stone's throw away. You come to on the trail, ears ringing, and go down off the crest.
trail.deer_lake_rim.fork.high.struck.ctx: Outcome: Stay high, fail, survived (Serious): on the crest at the High Divide junction

trail.deer_lake_rim.fork.high.fatal.text: The Divide is the tallest thing for some distance. This afternoon the storm comes to see the view as well.
trail.deer_lake_rim.fork.high.fatal.ctx: S6's stand-in death box (S24a builds the five screens; Appendix D 18b): its one button is Next, and a new hiker signs the guest book

trail.deer_lake_rim.fork.basin.clean.text: You go down the stone staircase as the first drops fall and sit out the thunder at Lunch Lake, with a jay for company.
trail.deer_lake_rim.fork.basin.clean.ctx: Outcome: the basin, clean (good): Lunch Lake about 2:31 pm

trail.deer_lake_rim.fork.basin.shaky.text: A boot skates on a wet step and you sit down hard. Nothing breaks but your dignity, which was never waterproof.
trail.deer_lake_rim.fork.basin.shaky.ctx: Outcome: the basin, shaky (a mishap, +10 min)

trail.deer_lake_rim.fork.basin.slip.text: You slide three steps on the seat of your pants. Finding your hat takes longer than the fall did.
trail.deer_lake_rim.fork.basin.slip.ctx: Outcome: the basin, fail, a slip (rung 1, +15 min)

trail.deer_lake_rim.fork.basin.sprain.text: Your ankle rolls on the last step. You limp down to Lunch Lake to wait out the storm, and the ankle.
trail.deer_lake_rim.fork.basin.sprain.ctx: Outcome: the basin, fail, a turned ankle (rung 2, +30 min)

trail.deer_lake_rim.fork.car.out.text: You turn your back on the storm and take the long way down. The thunder follows you as far as Deer Lake, then loses interest.
trail.deer_lake_rim.fork.car.out.ctx: Outcome: back to the car (sure, good): the Sol Duc trailhead about 5:42 pm

trail.odds.sure.ctx: A sure choice's tag, on the right of its button: no roll, nothing here can hurt the hiker (8.1)

trail.odds.fail.ctx: A diamond's fail share on its second line, in red: {share} is the share (fmt.pct), {what} the card's fail word (35% hit; 8.1, 12.2)

trail.odds.fatal.ctx: The fatal share, in red, after the fail share (0.7% fatal; 8.1, 8.7): rounded up, toward danger, and never 0

trail.odds.diamond.ctx: The red diamond's spoken name (VoiceOver), read with a diamond choice's label and odds (8.1)

trail.confirm.ask.ctx: A diamond's confirm, in place of its button, when it can't kill: {choice} is its label (12.1)

trail.confirm.fatal.ctx: A diamond's confirm when it carries a fatal share (12.1, 8.7)

trail.confirm.yes.ctx: The confirm's yes: the diamond is taken, and the compass spins (12.1, 8.8)

trail.confirm.no.ctx: The confirm's way back: the button comes back as it was (12.1)

trail.odds.intro.pct.text: The number is the chance this goes all right. The (i) shows the arithmetic.
trail.odds.intro.pct.ctx: The first % a player ever sees, one dry line before the box (8.7); the phone remembers it was shown

trail.odds.intro.diamond.text: A red diamond: this one could go badly wrong. The red number says how often.

trail.odds.intro.fatal.text: 'Fatal' means your hiker would die here, for good. There is always another way: look for 'sure'.
trail.odds.intro.fatal.ctx: The first fatal share; the sure choice beside it is outlined (8.7)

trail.odds.intro.sure.text: 'Sure' means nothing here can hurt you. It may cost time, or the trip.
trail.odds.intro.sure.ctx: The first sure tag (8.7 names it and gives no draft)

trail.why.title.ctx: The Why sheet's title (12.11): the bottom sheet behind a choice's (i), or a long press on it

trail.why.clean.ctx: The Why sheet's clean-chance row: p, the base and its modifiers, clamped 5 to 97 (8.5)

trail.why.made.ctx: The Why sheet's made-it row: clean plus shaky, the number on the button (8.8)

trail.why.bands.ctx: The three-band bar's legend (8.8): the bands' widths in points

trail.why.fatal.ctx: The fatal share's arithmetic (8.8): the fail share, the fatal band's share of the fails, the death roll, the exact product, and as shown, rounded up

trail.why.route.ctx: Where a choice goes and when, from the router (7.4 with breaks): Heart Lake about 4:26 pm, 3.4 mi

trail.why.exposed.text: On the open crest until about {time}
trail.why.exposed.ctx: How long a choice's way stays on the open crest (B.6: about 2:00 to 4:10)

trail.why.close.ctx: The close button of a sheet: the mailbox at the cabin (S7), and the Why sheet on the trail (12.11)

trail.why.crest_storm.ctx: A Why-sheet row: the base for staying on an exposed crest in a thunderstorm (content/rules/odds.json, B.6, 9.5)

trail.why.staircase.ctx: A Why-sheet row: the base for the stone staircase on dry rock (B.3)

trail.why.skill_footing.ctx: A Why-sheet row: the footing skill's modifier at the hiker's level, +2 a level (8.5; 12.11's River skill (level 1))

trail.compass.landed.ctx: The compass's result, spoken (a live region; the needle rests inside the band, never on the roll, 8.8): {band} is a band's name

trail.band.clean.ctx: A band's name: the compass's moss band, and the legend's (8.8)

trail.band.shaky.ctx: A band's name: the compass's pink band (made it, at a small cost)

trail.band.fail.ctx: A band's name: the compass's brick band (it goes badly)

trail.band.fatal.ctx: The fatal sliver at the far end of the brick band, spoken (8.8)

trail.outcome.good.ctx: The green fern ornament's spoken name, under an outcome's box (12.13)

trail.outcome.mishap.ctx: The brown twig ornament's spoken name (12.13: a mishap or setback)

trail.outcome.serious.ctx: The red diamond ornament's spoken name (12.13: serious or trip-ending)

trail.pencil.arrive.ctx: A pencil row under an outcome's box (12.13): where you got to, and when

trail.pencil.time.ctx: A pencil row: the time a band cost (12.13's Time -30m)
